name: Ida Kell

poster.hook: Thirty years in the Marrowby box. Hasn't let the lamp go out once.

flashback: What was the last thing you said to the stationmaster before he walked into the tunnel?

ifUnclaimed.npc: Ida stays in the signal box and keeps the lamp. Play her as the stubborn heart of the place: kind, short with fools, and writing things in the register she won't let anyone read.
cuts: Her letter (the register entry) can't be delivered; reveal it yourself when someone reads the register.

story.concept: The signalwoman. Fifty-eight, widowed, thirty years on this box. She believes in the timetable the way other people believe in God, and right now it's the only thing holding her up.
story.look: Railway-issue oilskin over a cardigan, lamp-black ground into her fingers, reading glasses on a string, a watch she winds every hour whether or not it matters.
carrying: the key to the lamp room
story.stake: The radio said the line must be clear. She's going to clear it.

ties.text: She has no memory of the 6:10 stopping on the second night, and she'd remember. She's watching him.
ties.public: doesn't believe he got off any train

ties.text: He reminds her of her son, and she's furious with herself for it.
ties.public: keeps giving him the last of the tea

keepsake.name: Ida's pocket watch
keepsake.note: Thirty years of trains, kept to the minute.
